group: Michigan Tech Planetary Surface Technology Development Lab (HuskyWorks / PSTDL)
why_they_are_a_fit: Owns a dusty thermal-vacuum chamber that already hits −196 °C / 10⁻⁶ torr with a 3,125-gallon LN2 tank. Finalist in both Break the Ice and Watts on the Moon. Built TEMPEST specifically for lunar-night power. Has student + alumni teams that already compete for prizes.
why_this_rank: Highest combined score: they already have the chamber, they already work the exact problem, they already enter prizes, and they can also host other competitors. First name to call. If they say yes the rest of the roster is easier.
best_contact_path: Direct email to the lab + Paul van Susante; also via Lunabotics / Watts alumni network
notes: Also a potential HOST chamber for the whole prize, not just a competitor. Dual-track them: enter, and/or host.

group: Carnegie Mellon Planetary Robotics Lab — MoonRanger
why_they_are_a_fit: Built a suitcase-sized lunar rover with a custom LN2-shrouded TVAC, xenon lamp, and a published cryo-shroud writeup. Thermal system is the team's published obsession. Students already know how to run long soaks overnight.
why_this_rank: They have already built the exact class of hardware (sub-10 kg, lunar thermal, self-powered) and the exact class of chamber. MoonRanger itself is not a night-survivor — that is the hook: 'your next paper is the night.'
best_contact_path: Lab site + William 'Red' Whittaker / current thermal leads via labs.ri.cmu.edu/moonranger
notes: Pitch as a follow-on to MoonRanger occultation work. They already published 'thermal safety during occultation' — this is the next increment.

group: Colorado School of Mines Center for Space Resources
why_they_are_a_fit: World's first dedicated Space Resources graduate program. Owns multiple dirty vacuum chambers (Apollo, Mercury, Viking) that reproduce lunar pressure and temperature. Hosts the Space Resources Roundtable. Adjacent to Orbital Mining Corp.
why_this_rank: Chamber + lunar-surface culture + a pipeline of graduate students who need a publishable hardware project. Also a recruiting node: one conversation here reaches a whole community.
best_contact_path: Angel Abbud-Madrid (aabbudma@mines.edu, 303-384-2300) or Christopher Dreyer (cdreyer@mines.edu, 303-273-3890)
notes: Ask them both to enter a student team AND to circulate the prize at the next Space Resources Roundtable.

group: UCSB Experimental Cosmology Group — Philip Lubin / H.E.L.P.S.
why_they_are_a_fit: Won the Watts on the Moon grand prize for a power-transmission + storage system designed to operate through lunar day and night. Already demonstrated hardware in a NASA Glenn vacuum chamber at PSR-like temperatures.
why_this_rank: They already beat NASA's night-power prize. A 1 kg hibernation payload is a natural, cheaper, public follow-on — and they have the prestige that makes other teams take the field seriously.
best_contact_path: Philip Lubin / UCSB experimental cosmology; Watts on the Moon alumni channel
notes: Their winning system was not 1 kg. Pitch the prize as a miniaturization / hibernation-architecture challenge, not a rematch.

group: Ohio State Electric Moon (Jin Wang / Wu Lu)
why_they_are_a_fit: Watts on the Moon final four. Built and field-tested a 6 km high-voltage transmission demo, then took it into NASA Glenn TVAC. Faculty-led with graduate students who already know prize mechanics.
why_this_rank: Proven prize competitors with lunar-night thermal hardware already in their lab. Slightly less 'lunar surface' identity than MTU/Mines/CMU, but the team exists and has done this.
best_contact_path: Jin Wang and Wu Lu
named_contact: ECE; OSU College of Engineering news desk as a warm intro
notes: https://engineering.osu.edu/news/2023/07/buckeyes-make-final-four-nasa-moon-mission-challenge
column17: Same pitch as UCSB: this is the hibernation-scale version of the problem they already solved at transmission scale.

group: Orbital Mining Corporation
why_they_are_a_fit: Watts on the Moon final four. Built a high-voltage DC converter that works through a sunless lunar night. Shares a building-ecosystem with Mines CSR and already used the Mines vacuum chamber for Lunar SCRUB dust work.
why_this_rank: Small enough that a public 1 kg demo is a useful credential, close enough to Mines that chamber access is solved, and already prize-fluent.
best_contact_path: Mines CSR intro (Abbud-Madrid / Dreyer) is the warmest path; also their own site / LinkedIn
named_contact: David Asner (CSO) via Mines partnership coverage
notes: Do not pitch them on dust — they are already doing that. Pitch the night-survival power electronics they already started for Watts.

group: Terra Engineering (Valerie & Todd Mendenhall)
why_they_are_a_fit: Husband-and-wife team. Won Break the Ice outright ($1M). NASA cited their rover as robust enough for south-pole conditions. Todd has been entering NASA prizes since the 2007 Regolith Excavation Challenge.
why_this_rank: The platonic prize competitor: small, serious, prize-fluent, and they just proved they will drive across the country to compete. A $5k purse is not why they would say yes — the public night-survival credential is.
has_own_tvac: no (used Marshall TVAC as a prize perk)
best_contact_path: NASA Centennial Challenges alumni channel; public coverage names both of them
notes: Lead with 'you were the team NASA said could survive the south pole — prove the night in public.' They do not have their own chamber; we have to broker one.

group: Starpath Robotics
why_they_are_a_fit: Break the Ice 2nd place. Already tested their rover inside Marshall's 20-foot TVAC. Building south-pole mining hardware that must survive darkness. ~30 people, still small enough that a public 1 kg demo is not beneath them.
why_this_rank: They have done the chamber, they work the environment, they are prize-fluent. Risk: they may consider $5k and open-source a distraction from a funded roadmap.
best_contact_path: Founders via starpath.space / LinkedIn; Break the Ice alumni channel
named_contact: Aakash Ramachandran (rover lead) / Josh Kavilaveettil named in NASA TVAC writeup
notes: Pitch as a cheap public credential for the night-survival claim their mining architecture depends on. Be ready for a no.

group: Cal Poly Aerospace — STELLA thermal vacuum chamber team
why_they_are_a_fit: Students just ran STELLA, their AFRL-funded TVAC, through its longest continuous cycle (24 h, overnight LN2 watch). The lab is actively looking for longer runs and external users.
why_this_rank: A student team that has already sat overnight with an LN2 shroud is 80% of the way to this prize. They want longer cycles; we are offering a 354-hour one with an audience.
best_contact_path: Cal Poly College of Engineering / STELLA faculty (Abercromby; Lubos Brieda)
notes: Also a candidate HOST chamber on the West Coast. Same dual-track as MTU.

group: Georgia Tech Space Systems Design Laboratory (Lightsey / Gunter / CSTAR)
why_they_are_a_fit: Owns a TVAC rated to 10⁻⁶ torr (Lightsey lab, 8 cu ft) plus a second campus chamber. Builds and flies CubeSats. Deep student pipeline.
why_this_rank: Classic CubeSat lab with a chamber on site. The 1 kg / beacon-at-dawn spec is a CubeSat thermal problem they already teach.
best_contact_path: ssdl.gatech.edu faculty pages; CSTAR as the institutional front door
notes: Pitch to a senior-design or CubeSat thermal subgroup

group: University of Michigan Exploration Laboratory (MXL)
why_they_are_a_fit: Flown multiple CubeSats (RAX, TBEx, MARIO). Clean room, vibe, ground stations. Uses campus SPRL for environmental test. Director previously ran Stanford SSDL.
why_this_rank: Flight-heritage CubeSat lab. They know cold-start electronics and beacons. Chamber is next door rather than in-house, which is still a solved problem.
best_contact_path: James W. Cutler, jwcutler@umich.edu, 734-615-7238; mxl-contact@umich.edu
notes: Cutler came from Stanford SSDL — he is also a node into the Stanford/Cal Poly CubeSat world.

group: Purdue CubeSat / High Vacuum Facility
why_they_are_a_fit: High Vacuum Facility in the Aerospace Sciences Lab (three chambers). Active CubeSat program. Lunabotics autonomy finalist (4th, 2026).
why_this_rank: Chamber + CubeSat + a prize-fluent student robotics culture. Easy to field a joint aero/EE team.
best_contact_path: engineering.purdue.edu/CubeSat; Lunabotics team advisor as a second door
notes: Use the Lunabotics team as the warm intro if the CubeSat faculty is slow.

group: University of Colorado Boulder — LASP / Aerospace senior projects
why_they_are_a_fit: LASP has four TVAC chambers open to external users and a SmallSat lab (Rick Kohnert). CU Boulder aero senior-design teams regularly build flight-like hardware. Adjacent to a dense Boulder/Golden lunar-startup cluster.
why_this_rank: The chambers are real and bookable. The competitor is more likely a student team using LASP than LASP staff themselves — still counts, and LASP can also be a host.
best_contact_path: Kush Tyagi (kush.tyagi@lasp.colorado.edu) for chambers; CU aero faculty for a student team; 303-492-6412 front desk
named_contact: Kush Tyagi (chambers) / CU aero senior-design coordinator
notes: Two asks: (1) a CU student team enters; (2) LASP considers hosting the common run.

group: UVA Mechatronics and Robotics Society (MARS) — 2026 Lunabotics champions
why_they_are_a_fit: Just won the 2026 Lunabotics Off-World Grand Prize and Innovation Award. Student-run, already in a build-test-compete cadence, coming off a public win.
why_this_rank: Highest-momentum student team in the country right now. They do not have a cryo TVAC, so we must broker access. They will take the meeting.
best_contact_path: UVA Engineering news desk / MARS officers; NASA Lunabotics staff can intro
notes: Off-season project pitch: 'your rover season just ended; this is a 1 kg box, not another rover.'

group: University of Alabama in Huntsville — Lunabotics autonomy + systems winners
why_they_are_a_fit: 1st in 2026 Lunabotics autonomy and systems-engineering paper. Sits next to Marshall Space Flight Center, which already hosted Break the Ice TVAC perks.
why_this_rank: Prize-fluent, in the one city on Earth where 'can we borrow a chamber' is a reasonable question. Marshall relationship is the hidden asset.
best_contact_path: UAH team advisor; Marshall Centennial Challenges alumni as a warm path
notes: If Marshall will not host the common run
column17: UAH is the team most likely to get a day in a Huntsville chamber anyway.

group: College of DuPage Lunabotics (2026 Construction 1st)
why_they_are_a_fit: Community-college team that beat research universities in construction. Student-run, scrappy, already ships hardware on a budget.
why_this_rank: The $5k purse and 'no radioisotopes, garage-buildable' framing is aimed at exactly this team. High yes-rate, lower chamber access.
best_contact_path: Team advisor via NASA Lunabotics guidebook contacts
notes: Pair them with a host chamber from day one or they stall.

group: New Mexico Tech Lunabotics (2026 Presentations 1st)
why_they_are_a_fit: 1st in 2026 presentations/demos. Socorro has a hands-on aerospace culture and is used to field hardware in harsh conditions.
why_this_rank: Solid student team, prize-fluent, likely to take a 1 kg thermal project as a senior-design. Chamber is the gap.
best_contact_path: Team advisor via Lunabotics

group: Michigan Tech Lunabotics (construction 3rd + PSTDL sibling)
why_they_are_a_fit: Separate from PSTDL/HuskyWorks but same campus. Construction 3rd and presentations honorable mention in 2026.
why_this_rank: If PSTDL enters as the lab, this is the student-only sibling team — useful as a second Houghton entry or as the actual student crew inside a PSTDL entry.
best_contact_path: Via PSTDL / van Susante
notes: Do not double-count with rank 1. Use as the student crew of a PSTDL entry unless they want their own slot.

group: Iowa State Lunabotics (comms-power award)
why_they_are_a_fit: Won the 2026 Efficient Use of Communications Power award — i.e. they already think about power budgets. Ames is an aerospace town.
why_this_rank: Power-budget fluency is the right instinct for a hibernation payload. Chamber access is the gap.
best_contact_path: Team advisor via Lunabotics

group: University of Utah Lunabotics (autonomy 3rd)
why_they_are_a_fit: 2026 autonomy 3rd. Utah has a growing smallsat scene (Utah State / SDL nearby).
why_this_rank: Autonomy team pivoting to thermal is a stretch, but they are prize-fluent and in a state with real environmental-test infrastructure at SDL.
best_contact_path: Team advisor; Space Dynamics Lab as a chamber conversation
notes: SDL is a government contractor lab — more likely a HOST than a competitor.

group: Northwestern / Laredo College / Virginia State / UIUC Lunabotics (systems-engineering awardees)
why_they_are_a_fit: 2026 systems-engineering paper and first-year awards. UIUC in particular has a deep aero program and a 2026 'Rocket Award' for systems-engineering mastery.
why_this_rank: Treat as a single outreach batch, not four separate pursuits. One well-written Lunabotics-alumni email to all four advisors.
best_contact_path: Batch email via NASA Lunabotics staff (they have the advisor list)
notes: One email. Do not spend a week on these until the top 10 have been called.

group: MIT Space Systems Lab / AeroAstro CubeSat groups
why_they_are_a_fit: World-class smallsat and space-systems lab. Students regularly build flight hardware. RASC-AL 2026 winners on lunar power (ECLIPSE) sit in the same department.
why_this_rank: Prestige if they enter. Risk: they are busy with real flight programs and may see $5k as not worth a faculty meeting. Still worth one well-aimed email because of the RASC-AL power team.
best_contact_path: AeroAstro faculty; the 2026 RASC-AL ECLIPSE team as the warm door
notes: Lead with the RASC-AL power team, not the whole SSL. 'You just designed lunar power on paper — build the 1 kg night-survival brick.'

group: Stanford Space Systems Development Lab (SSDL) / student smallsat groups
why_they_are_a_fit: Historic CubeSat lab (Cutler ran it before Michigan). Still produces student spacecraft. Bay Area hardware culture.
why_this_rank: Prestige + student energy. Same risk as MIT: faculty attention is expensive. One email, then move on.
best_contact_path: SSDL faculty / student leads; Cutler at Michigan can intro
notes: If Cutler (rank 11) is friendly
column17: ask him to make this intro.

group: Cal Poly CubeSat Lab (PolySat / CPCL) — distinct from STELLA
why_they_are_a_fit: One of the original CubeSat programs. Decades of flown spacecraft. Shares a campus with the STELLA chamber (rank 9).
why_this_rank: If STELLA's facility team does not enter, PolySat is the student group that should. Do not recruit both as separate roster slots unless they insist.
best_contact_path: PolySat / CPCL student director; Abercromby as the faculty bridge to STELLA
notes: Coordinate with rank 9 so Cal Poly fields ONE team.

group: USU / Space Dynamics Lab student + faculty groups
why_they_are_a_fit: SDL is a real environmental-test house (TVAC, vibe, thermal) attached to a university. Student teams can sometimes get leftover chamber time.
why_this_rank: More HOST than competitor, but a student team using SDL leftover time is a credible entry. One conversation covers both asks.
best_contact_path: USU aero faculty; SDL academic outreach
notes: Ask first whether they will host; enter second.

group: Embry-Riddle (Daytona + Prescott) smallsat / lunar teams
why_they_are_a_fit: Two campuses, both with spacecraft design programs. Prescott fielded a 2024 HuLC plume-mitigation team. Students are used to year-long hardware projects.
why_this_rank: Deep student bench and a culture of entering NASA student challenges. Chamber access varies by campus.
best_contact_path: Campus CubeSat / senior-design faculty at both sites
notes: One email per campus. Daytona is the more likely hardware shop.

group: Texas A&M / UT Austin / Rice student space systems teams
why_they_are_a_fit: Large aero programs, NASA JSC next door (Rice/UH/A&M pipeline), regular RASC-AL and Lunabotics participation.
why_this_rank: Treat as a Texas batch. High student energy, mixed chamber access. JSC leftover TVAC time is a fantasy — do not plan on it — but campus chambers and Houston commercial TVAC vendors exist.
best_contact_path: Batch to the three aero student-org advisors
notes: Space Grant office is the efficient node for all three.

group: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign aero / CubeSat
why_they_are_a_fit: 2026 Lunabotics Rocket Award. Large aero department. Has flown student spacecraft.
why_this_rank: Good student team, mid-tier chamber access. One email via the Lunabotics advisor.
best_contact_path: Lunabotics / CubeSat advisor

group: Astrolab (FLIP rover thermal team)
why_they_are_a_fit: FLIP is designed to hibernate through 100 hours of lunar night by actuating solar arrays over radiators. Flying on Griffin-1. Night survival is a current, public engineering problem for them.
why_this_rank: They are the most on-the-nose commercial team — and the least likely to enter a $5k open-source prize, because they are in flight test. Still worth one email: a 1 kg public demo of their hibernation architecture is cheap advertising if a junior engineer is allowed to run it.
best_contact_path: Jaret Matthews / FLIP thermal lead via astrolab.space
notes: Expect a no. The value of the email is (a) they say no but tweet the prize, or (b) a junior engineer enters as a side project.

group: Lunar Outpost (MAPP / Eagle thermal)
why_they_are_a_fit: Flew MAPP on IM-2. Building night-capable rovers. Same Golden cluster as Mines and Orbital Mining.
why_this_rank: Same as Astrolab: right problem, wrong incentive — unless a small internal team wants a public 1 kg result. One email, via the Mines cluster if possible.
best_contact_path: Mines CSR intro or Lunar Outpost academic outreach
notes: Better as a sponsor or judge than a competitor. Still ask.

group: ispace-U.S. (APEX / TENACIOUS thermal)
why_they_are_a_fit: Publicly collaborating with Zeno Power on lunar-night survival. Mission 3 (APEX 1.0) slated 2026. They care about this exact capability.
why_this_rank: Nuclear-path company; our prize bans radioisotopes. They will not enter as a corporate team. A US engineering intern team doing a non-nuclear 1 kg demo is the only plausible path.
best_contact_path: ispace-U.S. academic / intern program
notes: Do not pitch against Zeno. Pitch a non-nuclear student/intern side-car.

group: Firefly Aerospace Blue Ghost night-survival group
why_they_are_a_fit: Publicly working lander night-survival for longer CLPS missions.
why_this_rank: Wrong scale and wrong incentive. One courtesy email to their academic outreach; do not chase.
best_contact_path: Academic / payload-customer outreach
notes: Better as a future prize sponsor once generation 1 works.

group: Intuitive Machines night-survival / payload services
why_they_are_a_fit: Same as Firefly: lander-scale night survival is on their roadmap.
why_this_rank: Courtesy email only. They will not enter a 1 kg open-source prize.
best_contact_path: Payload services / academic outreach

group: Astrobotic Griffin / CubeRover thermal
why_they_are_a_fit: CubeRover is the closest commercial product to our 1 kg bar. Pittsburgh is also CMU MoonRanger territory — they already share a city with rank 2.
why_this_rank: CubeRover thermal engineers are the right humans; the company is the wrong buyer. One email, ideally via the CMU relationship so it does not die in a BD inbox.
best_contact_path: CMU intro
notes: https://www.astrobotic.com/
column17: Ask whether a CubeRover-class hibernation demo is something a junior engineer can run publicly. If no, ask them to tweet the prize.

group: ORBITBeyond (Power-as-a-Service / night survival)
why_they_are_a_fit: Selling lunar night-survival as a service for a 2029/2030 south-pole lander.
why_this_rank: They need the capability, they do not yet have flight hardware, and a public 1 kg demo is actually on-strategy for a company that is pre-lander. Dark-horse commercial entry.
best_contact_path: orbitbeyond.com contact / LinkedIn
notes: Worth a real conversation, not a courtesy email. They are early enough that a prize result is useful.

group: Advanced Cooling Technologies (ACT)
why_they_are_a_fit: Thermal-control hardware company; NASA collaboration awardee; heat pipes / PCM / cryo products are their catalog. A 1 kg hibernation payload is a demo unit they could assemble from stock.
why_this_rank: They sell the parts everyone else would buy. Entering themselves is a marketing decision. One email to their space-products lead.
best_contact_path: ACT space / aerospace products
notes: Better as a parts sponsor (heat pipes
column17: PCM) who also fields a house team.

group: Skycorp / Virtus Solis / X-Wheel (Watts on the Moon Phase 2 Level 1 alumni)
city: Santa Clara CA / Troy MI / Hialeah FL
why_they_are_a_fit: Three of the seven teams that won $200k in Watts Phase 2 Level 1. Already designed lunar-night energy systems. Not as famous as the final four, which is why they might still want a public win.
why_this_rank: Prize-fluent, already spent a year on this problem, and they did not take home the big trophy. Pride is a real recruiting lever.
best_contact_path: Watts on the Moon alumni list via NASA Centennial Challenges
named_contact: Team leads from the 2022 NASA announcement
notes: Batch email all three. Do not spend individual weeks on them until the final-four teams have answered.

group: Canopy Aerospace / Moonprint Solutions / KMI Space (NASA ACO / dust-and-thermal smalls)
why_they_are_a_fit: Recent NASA Announcement of Collaboration Opportunity awardees working lunar dust covers, thermal, and attachment. Small enough that a $5k public demo is a press release.
why_this_rank: Right size, adjacent problem. Night survival is a stretch from dust covers, but these are the 'we enter NASA things' shops.
best_contact_path: NASA ACO awardee list
notes: One batch email. Low priority until the Watts/Break-the-Ice alumni are exhausted.

group: City Labs (NanoTritium / BOHR)
why_they_are_a_fit: Flying a tritium betavoltaic in LEO; planning a tritium RHU. Night survival is their entire business — but it is nuclear, which our rules ban.
why_this_rank: They will not enter under our rules. They might still amplify the prize ('even the nuclear people say the non-nuclear path is worth proving'). One email, framed as a press/amplification ask, not an entry ask.
best_contact_path: Press / academic outreach
notes: Do not invite them to compete. Invite them to comment.

group: Zeno Power
why_they_are_a_fit: The company whose CEO called night survival 'the imperative.' Radioisotope systems. Collaborating with ispace-U.S.
why_this_rank: Same as City Labs: they define the problem in public and cannot enter our non-nuclear prize. Ask them to amplify.
best_contact_path: Tyler Bernstein / comms
notes: A quote from Bernstein on the prize page is worth more than an entry. Ask for that.

group: entX (RHU)
why_they_are_a_fit: Commercial RHU; flight-heritage demo planned Q4 2026 from Spaceport America.
why_this_rank: Banned by the radioisotope rule. Amplification / quote only.
best_contact_path: entX comms
notes: Same as Zeno: quote

group: Perpetual Atomics / University of Leicester americium RHU team
why_they_are_a_fit: Just produced the first Am-241 RHU core (ESA ENDURE). Deep cryo and radioisotope expertise.
why_this_rank: Banned as a competitor by the nuclear rule. Leicester's non-nuclear thermal group is a different conversation — see rank 55.
best_contact_path: University of Leicester space-nuclear comms
notes: If they have a student group doing non-nuclear hibernation

group: NASA Glenn lunar-hibernation electronics group (internal)
why_they_are_a_fit: The group that published the 50 K COTS cold-start architecture this prize is based on. They cannot enter a prize they inspired, but they are the ideal judge panel and the ideal quote.
why_this_rank: Not a competitor. Highest-value non-competitor in the entire landscape. Get them as judges / technical advisors before anyone else.
best_contact_path: NASA Glenn Space Power Workshop authors; TechPort project page
notes: Do this conversation in week 1. If Glenn will judge, every competitor takes the prize more seriously.

group: NASA Marshall Environmental Test Facility (V-20 TVAC)
why_they_are_a_fit: The 20-foot chamber that already hosted Starpath and was offered as a Break the Ice perk.
why_this_rank: Not a competitor. Highest-value HOST ask after MTU and Cal Poly. One conversation.
best_contact_path: Centennial Challenges staff (Naveen Vetcha) as the warm intro; ETF management
notes: Ask for leftover time, not a dedicated campaign. Even a 'we might host the common run' sentence in a press release is gold.

group: Resonate Testing (commercial TVAC, free-access competition)
why_they_are_a_fit: Already ran a free TVAC-access competition for New Space SMEs in Q1 2026. They give chamber time away as marketing.
why_this_rank: Not a competitor. Best commercial HOST prospect in Europe, and they have already demonstrated the exact behaviour we need (give away chamber time to make a name).
best_contact_path: resonatetesting.com/tvac-competition
notes: Ask them to be the European host node so non-US teams can run the same spec.

group: UCF CLASS / Exolith Lab + student teams
why_they_are_a_fit: Exolith is the simulant house; they hosted Lunabotics qualifying. Adjacent student CubeSat / planetary-science groups. Not a thermal lab first.
why_this_rank: Low as a competitor (wrong specialty) but high as a NETWORK — they talk to every Lunabotics team. Ask them to forward the prize, not to enter.
best_contact_path: Exolith / CLASS academic outreach
notes: Use as a distribution node for the Lunabotics batch (ranks 14–21).

group: Space Grant consortia (all 52) — as a distribution node
why_they_are_a_fit: Every Space Grant office has a mailing list of the exact student teams we want. This is not one competitor; it is the pipe.
why_this_rank: Send ONE well-written announcement to the National Space Grant Foundation and ask them to forward. Highest-leverage single email on this list after the top 10 direct asks.
best_contact_path: National Space Grant Foundation + state directors
notes: Do this the same week as the top-10 calls. It is how the long tail of student teams hears about the prize.

group: AIAA student branches at aero schools (batch)
why_they_are_a_fit: Every aero department has one. They need year-long projects.
why_this_rank: Same as Space Grant: one announcement
fit_for_1kg_non_nuclear_bar: not 50 conversations. The branches at schools already on this list will convert; the rest are lottery tickets.
best_contact_path: low
notes: https://www.aiaa.org/
column17: One email. Do not personalize beyond the schools in ranks 1–28.

group: Hackaday / Hackaday.io hardware community (as a channel + a few named builders)
why_they_are_a_fit: This is the community that already builds $200–$2,000 vacuum chambers and competes for $150 gift cards. A $5,000 purse with a 354-hour stream is a front-page story for them.
why_this_rank: Not one team — a channel that will produce 2–4 garage teams if the prize is written up on Hackaday. Highest-leverage earned-media ask in the GTM.
best_contact_path: Hackaday tips line + a project page on Hackaday.io; pitch the editors during recruitment, not at market open
notes: Named individuals to invite once the writeup lands: anyone who has published a TVAC build on Hackaday.io in the last 5 years. Scrape that list the week the article runs.

group: EEVblog / Applied Science / ElectroBOOM-adjacent hardware YouTubers
why_they_are_a_fit: Engineering YouTubers with vacuum, LN2, or cryo content. A 354-hour overnight stream is content they cannot buy.
why_this_rank: One well-targeted outreach per creator. Most will not enter; one of them filming their attempt is worth more than three silent university entries.
best_contact_path: YouTube / email / manager
notes: Do not spray. Pick 3–5 who have actually handled LN2 or vacuum on camera. Offer to cover consumables.

group: Arko Robotics / published hobby TVAC builders
why_they_are_a_fit: The well-known ~$200 near-space chamber writeup and its descendants. These people have already failed at the temperature we need and know it.
why_this_rank: High yes-rate, low chamber capability. Useful as 'The Rig' companion-prize entrants more than as Survive-the-Night entrants — unless they team with a lab.
best_contact_path: Blog comments / Hackaday project pages
notes: Redirect the best of these to The Rig (P2). If P2 is not running, invite them as a team that will use a host chamber.

group: UNISEC / university smallsat chapters outside the US (Japan, Europe, LatAm, Africa)
why_they_are_a_fit: UNISEC is the international CubeSat student network. They published the PeTT Peltier-TVAC paper. Chapters in Japan, Europe, and the Global South already build 1U thermal hardware.
why_this_rank: This is how the prize becomes international without us doing 40 country-specific outreach campaigns. One announcement through UNISEC-Global.
best_contact_path: UNISEC-Global secretariat / regional chapters
notes: Especially useful if Resonate (rank 45) will host a European run.

group: TU Delft / ESA BIC Delft / Dutch student smallsat (Delft-C3 heritage)
why_they_are_a_fit: One of Europe's strongest student spacecraft cultures. Nearby ESA ESTEC test facilities (we will not get those, but the students know how chambers work).
why_this_rank: Best single European student target if we want a non-US name on the roster. International roster is better television.
best_contact_path: TU Delft space engineering faculty / Delft Aerospace Rocket Engineering adjacent groups
notes: Pair with Resonate Testing (rank 45) so they have a chamber path that is not ESTEC.

group: ETH Zurich / EPFL Space Centers student groups
why_they_are_a_fit: Serious smallsat and robotics students, used to building flight-like hardware, comfortable with long experimental campaigns.
why_this_rank: High-quality European entry. Lower yes-rate than Delft because they are busier. One email each.
best_contact_path: EPFL Space Center / ETH student space teams

group: University of Leicester non-nuclear thermal / space systems students
why_they_are_a_fit: Same university as the americium RHU team, which means the campus has cryo culture. A student group doing non-nuclear hibernation would be a great story ('the other team at Leicester').
why_this_rank: Only worth it if a student group exists separately from the RHU work. One email to the space-systems teaching faculty.
best_contact_path: Leicester space-systems teaching faculty
notes: Do not pitch the RHU group. Pitch the students.

group: DLR / ESA student and young-professional networks (not the agencies)
why_they_are_a_fit: DLR built solar-sintered bricks and runs CoPhyLab / LUWEX TVAC work. The agencies will not enter; their student programs and young professionals might.
why_this_rank: Distribution node, not a competitor. One announcement into ESA Academy / DLR student programs.
best_contact_path: ESA Academy / DLR internship alumni lists
notes: If a named young-professional team forms, they jump up this list.

group: LunAres / Analog Astronaut Training Center / SAM (Biosphere 2) — analog habitat groups
why_they_are_a_fit: They live inside simulated missions and already think about night, power, and failure. They do not typically build cryo payloads.
why_this_rank: Wrong specialty for this prize (they are the Patch-the-Hab roster). One mention in a newsletter so a hardware-curious analog astronaut forwards it to their university lab.
best_contact_path: LunAres / AATC / SAM newsletters
notes: Do not spend real time. One paragraph in their newsletter.

group: Mars Society chapters + MDRS crews
why_they_are_a_fit: Same as analog habitats: enthusiastic
why_this_rank: not thermal engineers.
fit_for_1kg_non_nuclear_bar: Distribution only. The URC-adjacent chapters are already covered via rover-team outreach in the other GTM.
best_contact_path: low
notes: https://www.marssociety.org/
column17: Skip unless a chapter writes back.

group: MoonDAO citizens / Teams (house team)
why_they_are_a_fit: Already aligned. May form a team specifically so the community has a horse in the race. Chamber access is the gap — pair them with a host from ranks 1, 9, 13, or 45.
why_this_rank: Low technical starting point, high narrative value ('the community fielded a team'). Do not count them as one of the three must-have named competitors unless a real hardware lead steps up.
best_contact_path: Discord
notes: MoonDAO Discord #deprize
column18: Useful as a 4th or 5th roster slot, not as the anchor.

group: Random senior-design teams at any ABET aero/EE school (long tail)
why_they_are_a_fit: Hundreds of teams need a year-long project every September. Most will not finish. A few will.
why_this_rank: Do not pursue individually. The Space Grant + AIAA + Lunabotics-advisor emails (ranks 47, 48, 21) are how this tail hears about it. Anyone who replies gets a standard packet.
best_contact_path: Inbound only after the broadcast emails
notes: If more than three inbound senior-design teams appear, pick the one with a named faculty advisor who will sign a safety case.
